aiAudit.reason: The new private helper `createMockSession(Map<String, TestLsEntry[]> listResults)` creates a fresh `Session` mock per invocation (`Session session = mock(Session.class);`) and re-establishes exactly the same per-path stubs by iterating the supplied map (`when(session.list(entry.getKey())).thenReturn(entry.getValue());`), so no stub, matcher or argument binding is dropped or weakened and no mock instance is shared across tests. All 11 tests reported as sharing the `session.list(...)` stubbing (testLs, testLs_f, testLs_f_R, testLs_f_R_dirs, testLs_None, testLs_1, testLs_1_f, testLs_1_dirs, testLs_1_dirs_links, testLs_1_a_f_dirs_links, testLs_1_a_f_dirs_links_filtered) have their inline `mock(Session.class)` + `when(session.list(...)).thenReturn(...)` lines replaced by a `createMockSession(...)` call, so the duplication was genuinely removed rather than only abstracted. The only incidental changes are statement reordering (e.g. computing `files`/`level1..level3` before the mock) and the use of `Map.of`/`singletonMap`/`HashMap`, which is safe because the stubbed keys are distinct literals, so map iteration order cannot alter matching.

No stub, matcher, or answer was dropped or rebound: the mocks are plain, unstubbed `mock()` instances and no test verifies interactions or asserts on mock identity, so the same pass/fail outcomes are expected. In `notificationWithFilter` the two formerly distinct mocks (bean factory and event source) are now the same instance, but the test asserts only on received message content/headers, not on mock identity or interaction counts, so this is not an observable defect.

aiAudit.reason: The new helper `createMockSocket(InputStream, InetAddress)` creates a fresh `mock(Socket.class)` per invocation and applies exactly the two original stubbings (`getInputStream()` -> the passed stream, `getInetAddress()` -> the passed address), so no stub was dropped, weakened, or re-bound to different arguments. All three call sites were actually converted: testNetClient and testNetClientSocketTimeout use `Socket socket = createMockSocket(is, inetAddress);`, and testNetServer uses `Socket socket = createMockSocket(is, inetAddress); Socket socket1 = createMockSocket(is, inetAddress);`, preserving two distinct mock instances for `socket` and `socket1` rather than sharing one. The untouched `doThrow(new SocketTimeoutException()).when(socket).connect(any(), eq(1000));` still binds to the helper-produced instance. Statement reordering (creating `is`/`inetAddress` before the socket stubs) is inert because neither interacts with the socket mock, and each test still declares `throws Exception`, so the helper's `throws Exception` is satisfied.

aiAudit.reason: The extracted helper `createMockFolder` calls `mock(folderClass)` on every invocation, so no mock instance is shared between test cases. Each stubbing it absorbs is byte-for-byte equivalent to the original: `given(folder.getPermanentFlags()).willReturn(new Flags(Flags.Flag.USER))`, `given(folder.isOpen()).willReturn(true)`, and `willAnswer(invocation -> messages).given(folder).search(any(SearchTerm.class))`, with the `messages` array now supplied as a parameter holding the same value the lambda previously captured. The one test-specific extra stub, `given(folder.exists()).willReturn(true)` in testIdleChannelAdapterException, is retained at the call site, and the mock class is still `IMAPFolder.class` there because the class is passed through. All five listed call sites were replaced by `createMockFolder(...)`, so the duplication was genuinely removed; the reordering of the `folderField`/`storeField` reflection setup is call-order irrelevant since `adapter.start()` and `receiver.receive()` still run last.

Reordering `makeMockConnection()` before the factory mock has no observable effect since the two mocks are independent and no test asserts on aggregate mock-creation interactions.
